title: api-gateway: tighten streaming proxy buffers and routing payload limits to stabilize function/tool calling and OpenAI compat
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: We observed intermittent OOMs and elevated latencies on the API gateway during high-concurrency streaming function/tool-calling workloads. Root cause analysis pointed to two contributing factors: unbounded per-connection proxy buffers and lenient per-route payload thresholds that allowed large tool call/structured outputs to be routed through the streaming proxy. This PR tightens proxy buffer sizing, enforces per-route streaming payload limits with graceful fallback, and updates the OpenAI-compat streaming adapter to preserve chunk boundaries while returning early errors for oversized payloads.

What changed: 1) Streaming proxy: introduced configurable max buffer per connection (default 256KB) and backpressure heuristics to drop/trim non-essential buffered frames for long-tail connections. 2) Routing/payload limits: added per-route streaming_payload_max_bytes (default 2_000_000) and server-side early rejection with 413-style metadata for OpenAI-compat endpoints. 3) OpenAI compatibility: adapter now preserves chunk boundaries and emits partial-response metadata when fallback occurs so SDKs can handle truncated tool outputs. 4) Observability: new metrics (api_gateway.proxy_buffer_bytes, api_gateway.streaming_rejections_total, api_gateway.fallbacks_total) and dashboards updated. 5) Tests & rollout: added integration tests for chunking, size rejection, and canary deployment config (5% -> 20% -> 100%).

Compatibility notes: This introduces stricter defaults for streaming payloads; existing customers with >2MB streaming messages will see 413-style rejections until they opt-in to a higher per-route limit or route large uploads through the non-streaming upload endpoint. The OpenAI-compat layer behavior changes the shape of partial responses in failure cases (we document the metadata field partial_response=true). The change is conservative (defaults tightened) and accompanied by admin config and runtime flags to opt out.

Testing: unit tests for buffer heuristics, end-to-end integration tests validating tool-call streaming with chunk-preservation and rejection, load test showing 30% reduction in peak gateway memory under synthetic tool-calling load, and smoke tests for SDKs (python/ts) compat. CI: all checks passed after one flaky integration test rerun.

Rollout plan: canary at 5% traffic for 48h observing memory/latency and streaming_rejections_total; increase to 20% then 100% over a week. Support will monitor the new metrics and coordinate with top customers to raise per-route limits if needed.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration tests added - [x] Metrics instrumented - [x] Docs updated - [x] Canary config included
commits: add: streaming proxy per-connection buffer & backpressure heuristics
feat: enforce per-route streaming_payload_max_bytes with 413 early rejection
fix(openai-compat): preserve chunk boundaries and emit partial_response metadata
test: add integration tests for streaming chunking and size rejection
docs: document streaming limits and fallback behavior
ops: add canary deployment config and dashboard updates
review_comments: Mateo Ruiz (review): Buffer heuristic looks reasonable, but can we make the default conservative and add a node-level override? Requested change: expose NODE.streaming_proxy_max_buffer_mb as an override.
Asha Patel (reply): Added node-level override and documented it in docs/api-gateway/limits.md. Kept the conservative default at 256KB. PTAL.
Priya Singh (review): Please add an integration test that simulates a long-lived slow consumer so we can validate buffer trimming behavior.
Asha Patel (reply): Added integration test 'streaming_compat_test.go::TestSlowConsumerBufferTrim' and load test results to the PR description.
Evan Liu (approval): Verified canary dashboard and metrics. Approving — behavior is well-documented and has admin overrides.
release_notes: Tighten API gateway streaming defaults: reduced default per-connection proxy buffer (256KB), enforce per-route streaming payload limit (2MB) with graceful 413-style early rejection, preserve chunk boundaries for OpenAI compatibility, added metrics and canary rollout config. Admin override available for legacy large-stream workloads.
